premises.statement: Augustine's cited counsel is presented as concerning killing to avoid being killed, with a public-role qualification.
The second objection treats bodily life as a loss one may suffer unwillingly, and therefore contemptible for its argument.
The third objection reads a clerical warning as denying license to kill.
The fourth objection invokes spiritual-life priority and compares homicide with other mortal sins.
The fifth objection invokes the tree-and-fruit inference about defense and its effect.
The sed contra compares defense of a house with defense of life.
One act may have two effects, one intended and one beyond intention.
Moral acts receive their species from what is intended rather than an incidental effect.
Good intention does not excuse force disproportionate to its end.
Intended killing is reserved to public authority for the common good, and public actors may still act from private passion.
The respondeo states a comparative priority for providing for one's own life over the attacker's life.
Augustine's authority is scoped to intending to kill to free oneself from death.
The second reply reads “for these things” as designating intention.
Irregularity follows a homicide act even without sin or intended killing.
Fornication/adultery is not ordered by necessity to preserving one's life, unlike an act from which homicide sometimes follows.
The fifth reply reads the cited prohibition as addressing vindictive retaliation.

limitations: Every source_principle is an expressly declared assumption attached through model-level @source metadata to a named SUMMA_Q64_A7_* section anchor; this is model provenance, not a claim that native proof sourceAnchors are populated or that a philosophical premise is independently proven.

The death-as-means to intended-death transition is a conservative lexical bridge declared by the reconstruction; explicit negative intention remains visible as BOTH and does not silently count as incidental death.
The sed contra house-to-life analogy is inventoried as a source premise; no transfer rule or resolution of its bridge is asserted.
The ad 3 model keeps irregularitas distinct from moral culpability by querying moral_culpability through an explicit negative literal.

Public authority and common-good orientation remain separate from private passion; a public role does not erase private passion. Conditional permission branches also require self_defense_act and the external vis_moderata judgment.
The model distinguishes intended killing from an unintended death, and revenge from moderated defense.
Finite scenarios cannot establish a universal no-regress principle or discharge unrepresented philosophical bridges.
This is an experimental article-local reconstruction, not full-article acceptance; fullArticleVerified remains false.
The Augustine scope path requires a case fact that killing is intended as a means to free oneself from death; generic intended death alone is insufficient.
Incidental killing uses an explicit negative literal for intended_effect; absence of a positive intent fact is not treated as evidence of non-intention.
The three conditional normative heads are derived rules only; no fixture asserts them as facts.

The argumentation query models only the scoped arg. 1/ad 1 intermediate; it makes no hard-coded priority claim and must be reviewed with skippedRules and resource-limit output when execution is available.
The source principle favoring provision for one’s own life is registered as a source premise; its independent justification remains open.

Proportionality is one external adjudicated input vis_moderata: absence requests judgment; explicit negation supports the excessive-force branch; a BOTH conflict is retained on the judgment itself and blocks both downstream branches under §§65–66, leaving their conclusions NEITHER/COMPUTED.

The arg. 1/ad 1 argumentation tests expose the queried class, but their simple test summaries do not retain skippedRules; coordinator review requires a canonical argumentation document before promotion.

A prior expectation that downstream conclusions were TRUE_ONLY under a BOTH vis_moderata judgment was corrected to NEITHER/COMPUTED in accordance with §§65–66; the direct BOTH judgment query is retained. The earlier failed snapshot and this correction history are preserved.
